title: Three Winters and One Short Nail
subtitle: 家庭生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 家庭生活（人与自我·生活与家居）
meta: 主题语境：家庭生活（人与自我·生活与家居）　|　核心词汇：furniture　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 furniture 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1961 my grandmother ① moved the furniture that no neighbour in the street would have counted, and she said the moving was the whole of the winter. The ② furniture, meaning the chairs themselves and not the room, ran three winters and stayed uncounted in the book; furniture, she said, is the only thing in a street that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ piece of furniture in that house had the same short nail beside it, and the ④ furniture at the far end, meaning the part they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only part anybody ever thanked twice. Furniture, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; my grandmother said the counting is the part that fills three winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the furniture was the whole of the matter, meaning the fittings and not the chairs. The ⑥ furniture, meaning the fittings and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; furniture, he said, is either something you move or the only word that means both chairs and fittings. He said the fittings are the part they remember.

By 1968 the ⑦ furniture had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short nail. The ⑧ furniture of the whole thing, my grandmother wrote in January, was one street and three winters of counting; furniture, she said, is either the part at the far end or the reason you learned to count. She said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ furniture I remember is the part counted in the plan, which closed in 1970 and is still described as the quietest in the street. ⑩ Furniture, my mother said in 1972, is the only thing that improves by being counted; all furniture, she said, is fittings that have agreed to look like chairs. She said the fittings were the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 家具（指屋子里每一件旁边的那一件）
B. n. 家具（指那些椅子本身，与房间相对）
C. 固定搭配：move the furniture 搬动家具
D. n. 家具（指留给孩子们的那一部分）
E. n. 家具（抽象总称，指一条街上的搬迁之事）
F. n. 家具（指计划里写到、被清点过的那一部分）
G. n. 附件；配件；陈设（指装配在房屋里的构件，指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）
H. n. 配件（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）

items.q: moved the furniture that no neighbour in the street would have counted
The furniture, meaning the chairs themselves and not the room
Every piece of furniture in that house
the furniture at the far end
the furniture was the whole of the matter
the furniture had become a line in a plan
The furniture of the whole thing

answers.why: move the furniture 意为“搬动家具”，1961 年祖母搬动了街上没有一位邻居肯清点的家具。
furniture 意为“家具”，指那些椅子本身而不是房间，它经过了三个冬天而在簿子上没有被清点。
furniture 意为“家具”，指屋子里每一件旁边的那一件，每一件旁边都有同一枚短短的钉子。
furniture 意为“家具”，指留给孩子们的那一部分，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
furniture 意为“附件、配件、陈设”，指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西，叔叔说这些构件就是那件事的全部。
furniture 意为“配件”，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西而不是那些家具，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
furniture 意为“家具”，指计划里写到、被清点过的那一部分，到 1968 年这一部分成了计划里的一行。
furniture 意为“家具”，祖母一月写道，整件事的搬迁之事是一条街道和三个冬天的清点。
furniture 意为“家具”，我记得的是计划里清点过的那一部分，1970 年结束了，至今仍被说成街上最安静的一部分。
furniture 为抽象总称，母亲 1972 年说，家具是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的东西。
